summary: WAN optimizer DNS suffix injection causes control-plane hostname to resolve to internal IP -> certname mismatch / mtls auth loop
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that control-plane mTLS auth intermittently fails from branch-office clients. Symptoms are TLS handshake failures and repeated control-plane credential refresh loops.

Impact:
- BlueWave production inference agents across two branch routers fail to establish persistent control-plane sessions; request rate for those agents drops ~60%.
- Customer sees repeated token refresh attempts in logs and increased error surface in application.

Environment:
- Private deployment (Redwood Private) with VPC peering to customer on-prem via SD-WAN + WAN optimizer appliance.
- Affected hosts: branch agent fleet (10 hosts), all in us-east-1 peering region.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) From a branch agent VM, curl https://controlplane.redwood-inference.internal:443/health (agent uses mTLS, curl used with -k to observe TCP/TLS behavior).
2) Observe TLS alert "certificate verify failed: hostname mismatch" or agent log showing "control-plane auth: certname mismatch".
3) Restart network stack or flush DNS cache on the appliance -> resolution lasts minutes to hours then recurs.

Observed logs (snippets customer supplied):
- agent.log: "auth: handshake failed: x509: certificate is valid for controlplane.prod.redwood-inference.com, not controlplane.internal.local"
- tcpdump (agent side): DNS answer contains A record 10.50.8.22 for controlplane.redwood-inference.internal TTL 300
- appliance syslog: "dns-suffix-inject: appended search suffix 'internal.local' to queries for 'controlplane'"

Temporary mitigation noted by customer:
- Flushing DNS cache on WAN optimizer returns correct public A record and control-plane sessions re-establish until the appliance re-injects suffixes (typically after idle period or routing flaps).

Additional notes:
- Customer uses split-horizon DNS internally for some services. PRVs (proxy/resolver) on their WAN optimizer are doing dynamic suffix injection to try to satisfy short hostnames; this behavior appears to be resolving our control-plane hostname to an internal IP and/or rewriting the query to a local domain.

Requested outcome:
- Permanent fix or recommended configuration to stop suffix injection for the control-plane hostname; advice on recommended NAT/DNS rules or iptable exceptions until customer onboarding update can be applied.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:08 - Support initial triage: verified customer's logs show DNS answers for 'controlplane.redwood-inference.internal' returning 10.50.8.22 with TTL 300; certificate CN/altNames do not include that address -> mismatch.

2026-03-10 10:21 - SRE ran remote capture (pcap) supplied by customer; observed query rewriting: original query 'controlplane.redwood-inference.internal' -> appliance rewrites to 'controlplane.internal.local' and returns internal A. Hypothesis: WAN optimizer is performing search-suffix addition + answer-synthesis for short names or configured host overrides.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Confirmed control-plane public IPs serve valid certificate for controlplane.prod.redwood-inference.com. Verified control-plane hostname served to customer should be FQDN matching cert (we enforce SANs that reference prod domain).

2026-03-11 08:30 - Asked customer for appliance config snippet; they provided ACL and DNS policy entries. Found rule with 'append-suffix internal.local' and a 'local-resolve' enabled. This appears to run after 2s timeout of external resolver causing caching of internal answer.

2026-03-11 12:42 - Reproduced similar behavior in lab by deploying a DNS forwarder that appends search suffix and responds to unresolved queries with a local A; agent library falls back to that A and fails mtls. Created reproducer: nslookup -> shows rewrite; openssl s_client -> cert CN mismatch.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:45 - Laura Chen (Support): Thank you BlueWave, we've escalated to SRE. Can you confirm number of affected hosts and whether this is limited to branch router cluster A?

2026-03-10 10:05 - BlueWave NetOps (customer): Affected hosts are two branch locations (NYC and ATL) behind the same model of WAN optimizer; around 10 agents total. We'll provide appliance logs and resistor config in the next message.

2026-03-10 11:15 - Marco Rivera (SRE): We see DNS answer rewrite; hypothesis is suffix injection + local-resolve. Requesting the appliance DNS policy and NAT rules. Also requesting tcpdump of the query/response with TLS handshake captured from an affected agent.
2026-03-11 09:00 - BlueWave NetOps: Uploaded appliance config (anonymized) and pcap to S3: s3://bluewave-support/553179/pcap-0311.pcap (provided presigned link).

2026-03-11 15:12 - Marco Rivera (SRE): Confirmed reproducer in lab. Patch suggestion: on the appliance disable suffix-injection for the redwood control-plane FQDN or add controlplane.redwood-inference.internal to 'do-not-suffix' list. Also recommend creating a static host override pointing to the public control-plane IP.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer added 'no-suffix' rule and a host override in WAN optimizer for controlplane.redwood-inference.internal pointing to external IP. After change, agents re-established control-plane sessions and error rate dropped to baseline.\nPermanent recommendation: Customer to update WAN optimizer policy to exclude vendor control-plane FQDNs from dynamic suffixing and synthetic responses. We provided a short config diff and example ACLs.\nFollow-up: SRE to add a note in Private Deploy runbook (infra/runbooks#12) recommending explicit host-exclude examples for common control-plane and artifact hostnames.
postmortem_followup_items: Add 'controlplane.*redwood-inference*' examples to Private Deploy DNS troubleshooting runbook
Update onboarding checklist to ask for list of middleboxes that rewrite DNS and request 'do-not-suffix' entries for control-plane/asset hostnames
Consider adding client-side validation: warn on certificate subject mismatch and include helper for detecting local-synthesized answers in agent diagnostics
